abstract: Transporters localized to the small intestinal epithelium govern the absorption of many orally administered drugs and nutrients, and thorough characterization of transporter protein abundance is key to accurate prediction of small molecule absorption. Previous studies have reported more than 100 solute carrier (SLC) and ATP-binding cassette (ABC) superfamily transporters expressed in the intestine, but only a small subset of these proteins have been quantified in native intestinal tissue. In addition, a majority of published transporter abundance data for the intestine were collected with adult tissue. Here, we report the identification and relative quantification of 87 SLC and 18 ABC superfamily transporters by intestinal region in neonatal, pediatric, and adult small intestinal mucosa using data-independent acquisition-mass spectrometry. This study identified transporters, including SLC10A2, uniquely expressed by intestinal region in all 3 age groups, and region-associated abundance for 23 SLC/ABC transporters in pediatrics and adults. The protein abundance data reported here provide a valuable resource for the prediction of nutrient and drug absorption and efflux across age and will inform future studies of specific transporters and age-associated differences in transporter abundance. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study reported the relative abundance of key xenobiotic transporters along the length of the small intestine in neonates, pediatrics, and adults based on data-independent acquisition-mass spectrometry. Intestinal region-associated transporter protein expression was observed for drug transporters and understudied nutrient transporters across age groups.
